title: epan: Make AT_NUMERIC behave more safely
description:
Implement a better handling of byte sizes as well as preventing
possible memory bleeds

Fixes: #18147

notes.body: assigned to @rknall

%llu should be replaced by PRIu64 for portability

If you assume that little endian is used, you should use pletohXX functions

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7228/diffs?diff_id=422034686&start_sha=3b566aac320b33b5fce46388ce6746dc5dcb0d12#4e4e1cc0dd9e1169dc173fbb386b883af564443e_552_552)

The comment text in `address.h` should more accurately say "host endian" instead of "little endian" because there is no conversion wanted or needed, it's just a variable-sized unsigned value within the address data.

  • 251c1568 - epan: Make AT_NUMERIC behave more safely
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7228/diffs?diff_id=422034686&start_sha=3b566aac320b33b5fce46388ce6746dc5dcb0d12)

But this allocator is not enforceable, right? Basically everyone who wants to use AT_NUMERIC would have to write the same allocator and ensure that all 64bit are allocated?

Or am I missing something here?

Ok, now I get it. But in this case I would put an assert in alloc_address_wmem to ensure, that it is no longer used for AT_NUMERIC, to avoid implementing a dissector where people still use the older _wmem version but than probably not addressing enough space and therefore causing memory bleeds again. But that would introduce more complexity for the user to implement instead.

So by doing it without a second alloc_x and having the complexity inside numeric_addr_to_str the user will not need to know that and it makes it easier to handle in a dissector. Basically it reduces the complexity in using the API in comparison to the complexity of the implementation in address_types.c. 

Hope this makes sense ;-)
Seems inconvenient for everybody to have to handle 4 cases to be able to manipulate AT_NUMERIC addresses. But OK, as you wish.

Your original dereference uses host-endian values but the doc said otherwise.

This change now requires the encoded values to be little endian, which disagrees with the documentation change in `address.h`. It seems like keeping everything in host endian and using dereference (i.e. `*((guint64*)...`) is the easiest to understand because the user side (setting the address) is just a mem copy.

At this point I am inclined to change the documentation rather than the implementation. Using that method makes the code a little bit safer in my opinion. But you are correct, it means the documentation has to be changed

I can assure you, this is correct. I have tried that code with about 20 different trace files now, and it works exactly as intended. 0x3FF is the openSAFETY broadcast address. On hindsight, there is a define for that, which should be used instead

The base use case for AT_NUMERIC is that there are protocols out there which have numeric values that are being generated from other information out of the protocol. In case of openSAFETY, the address is partly encoded in 10 bytes. 

To be fair, I have only tested it with openSAFETY and EPL (change coming). There can be use cases out there, which work differently. Sample traces can be found at https://wiki.wireshark.org/SampleCaptures#opensafety
It works only because your machine is little-endian.
Your reply explains the use case for AT_NUMERIC. I get that but not why little-endian byte order was chosen specifically.

You are correct in that assumption, and I do not disagree with that. As I said, those protocols are the only ones tested and they are only being used on little-endian systems. There is no big-endian implementation, nor will their be one. Although the stacks are prepared for it, there is a lot of things in the background that need to work for them being big-endian.

That being said, I am still concerned about the point you raised. I think it is a valid point and that could lead to issues going forward. Would it be sufficient from your POV, if we specifically hint about it being little-endian?

The original idea you proposed, although it might not suffer from the same issue, has another side-effect. If indeed you would get a trace that contains AT_NUMERICs in both little-endian and big-endian, than the UI would not know how to properly display those. Mixed filters applying to both might fail or the numbers might not be displayed correctly. Sorting will most certainly fail, as most user machines are little-endian. I am in favor of having the stuff stored little-endian but the longer I think about it, it seems to lack finesse that way.
I will push an MR and add you as reviewer. Then you can tell me what you think. I won't change the 4 cases printf(), that's not the issue right now.
Sounds like a good idea. I appreciate the help. I must admit, I feel a lot more safe in the UI parts of the code, thane epan ;-)

@rknall Did you forget to amend the [TrafficDataFilterProxy](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/ui/qt/widgets/traffic_tab.cpp#L123) class?
No, it’s in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/ui/qt/widgets/traffic_tab.h

I mean the sorting of AT_NUMERIC in the traffic tables cannot handle the full 64 bits. I don't know why you are pointing me to the header file.

I had to dig into the Qt code but I wasn't wrong. QString::toInt() will overflow with a value greater than 0x7FFFFFFF (it returns 0).
Ah yes, now I got you. Sorry, I was preoccupied with the kids. I am currently preparing a change for those places where it is required

changes_data.diff:
@@ -28,6 +28,12 @@ extern "C" {
  * If an address type is added here, it must be "registered" within address_types.c
  * For dissector address types, just use the address_type_dissector_register function
  * from address_types.h
+ *
+ * AT_NUMERIC - a numeric address type can consist of a guint8, guint16, guint32 or guint64
+ * little-endian value. If no correct length is provided, to avoid data bleed, a guint8 is
+ * assumed. If the value represented is originating from a big-endian system, it is the
+ * responsibility of the dissector to do the proper conversion. Only representation (aka
+ * conversion of value to string) is implemented for this type.
  */
 typedef enum {
     AT_NONE,               /* no link-layer address */
@@ -42,7 +48,7 @@ typedef enum {
     AT_IB,                 /* Infiniband GID/LID */
     AT_AX25,               /* AX.25 */
     AT_VINES,              /* Banyan Vines address */
-    AT_NUMERIC,            /* Numeric address type */
+    AT_NUMERIC,            /* Numeric address type. */
 
     AT_END_OF_LIST         /* Must be last in list */
 } address_type;
